statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l and a compactification c=(j,p) of a morphism f:X→Y. Let o be the section-normalized IntegralOpenReduction.Operations for j [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison], d the finite proper direct-image comparison data normalized on sections and K-injective representatives, and e the finite open scalar-comparison data normalized on extension summands [lem-sf-compact-support-proper-image-tower]. Then (i) at every finite exponent the slice extension o.finiteExtension is naturally isomorphic to the intrinsic finite extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero]; and (ii) for every derived-complete K, the ordinary-image tower sfDirectImageTransition for p applied to the completed extension j_!K [def-weil-derived-direct-image] is naturally isomorphic to the slice properTower, while the slice supportTower is naturally isomorphic to the specified intrinsic compact-support tower [def-sf-integral-compact-support-tower]. These are isomorphisms of whole inverse systems, not just levelwise object isomorphisms. No constructibility or finite-field hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Obtain the finite open comparison family with its ordinary coefficient compatibility from sfFiniteOpenPresentation. Each member supplies the finite-extension Nonempty conclusion. The adjacent quotient comparison in that module is proved directly from ofOpSequence.

Finite ordinary direct-image functors are definitionally equal. For the completed extension of any K, sfDirectImageTransition_presentation identifies the ordinary adjacent transition with properTransition. Use the identity isomorphisms as level comparisons.

Construct each support level comparison by exact localization of the supplied finite open natural isomorphism followed by finite derived direct image and completed restriction. sfSupportTransition_presentation, applied to its ordinary coefficient compatibility, gives the adjacent support square.

Use NatTrans.ofOpSequence to extend each adjacent square to naturality for every arrow in ℕᵒᵖ. Every component is an isomorphism, so NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app and asIso give the required two system isomorphisms. This is proved by the private towerIsoOfSteps helper. No equality of morphisms in a derived system category is inferred merely from evaluations.

proof_origin.place: Definition 6.7.6 and the existing Steps 1--6; formal assembly from the finite ordinary coefficient square and the two adjacent-arrow identities, using NatTrans.ofOpSequence.

lean.statement: theorem sfCompactSupportTower_presentation (c : Compactification f) (o : IntegralOpenReduction.Operations l E c.i) (d : CompactSupportProperImageTower.DirectData l E c.g) (e : CompactSupportProperImageTower.OpenData l E c.i o) : (∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty (IntegralOpenReduction.finiteExtension l E c.i o n ≅ sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero c.i (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))) ∧ ∀ K : (IntegralOpenReduction.complete l E X).FullSubcategory, Nonempty (Functor.ofOpSequence (sfDirectImageTransition l E c.g ((IntegralOpenReduction.shriek l E c.i o).obj K.obj)) ≅ CompactSupportProperImageTower.properTower l E c.i c.g o (d := d) K.obj) ∧ Nonempty (CompactSupportProperImageTower.supportTower l E c.i c.g o (d := d) e K.obj ≅ Functor.ofOpSequence (sfCompactSupportTransition l E c K.obj))
